name: CHROMEWORKS Auris Focal Directional Hearing Suite
description:
The Auris Focal replaces the standard cochlear architecture with a phased-array microphone cluster and a precision neural encoder capable of isolating individual sound sources up to 240 meters in complex acoustic environments. A companion AI kernel runs continuous spectral separation, allowing the user to 'pin' a specific voice or sound signature and track it through ambient noise, crowd chatter, or active countermeasures. The system integrates seamlessly with CHROMEWORKS' neural mesh platform and supports up to twelve simultaneous pinned audio channels.

Favored by corporate investigators, surveillance operatives, and high-end security contractors who need intelligence-grade audio awareness without the bulk of external equipment. On the Tier 3-4 social circuit it has also found a niche among journalists and legal professionals who want irrefutable recall of private conversations, a practice that sits in a legally grey area throughout GLMZ.
installation_requirements: Microsurgical cochlear replacement, bilateral preferred; CHROMEWORKS-certified audiological clinic; 48-hour neural calibration period post-op
rejection_risk: Low — biocompatible titanium housing with CHROMEWORKS' proprietary neuro-silk electrode array reduces inflammation response
maintenance: Software updates quarterly via clinic uplink; physical inspection annually; electrode array replacement every 4-5 years

side_effects: Initial 2-4 week hypersensitivity period causing sensory headaches in loud environments
Occasional phantom audio artifacts when AI kernel misidentifies overlapping sound signatures
Difficulty sleeping without active dampening mode enabled
Minor tinnitus flare-up if firmware is outdated
cultural_context: In GLMZ's Shelf and Stack tiers, owning a Chromeworks implant of any kind is a status signal — the Auris Focal's subtle chrome-finish receiver port behind the ear is recognized as a mark of someone with serious money or serious connections. Corporate security firms often subsidize installation as a condition of employment, making it both a tool and a brand of loyalty.
known_users: Wealthy paranoid executives who distrust their own staff
story_hooks: A user's pinned audio channel keeps returning fragments of a conversation that hasn't happened yet — possibly a firmware exploit, possibly something worse
A journalist's Auris Focal recorded something it shouldn't have, and now someone is trying to surgically remove it from her skull without her consent
A black market firmware patch promises to extend range to 600m, but every user who installs it goes deaf in one ear within a week
